accent.description: call-to-action colour (primary buttons, form submits); unset = the primary.

canvas.description: page ground behind the sections; unset = the platform ground.

backgroundImage.description: A picture behind the component: asset:<id> of an uploaded image, or null. Upload the image to the app first and use its asset id; a web address is not accepted. The picture sits under the content and follows the corners of the box. Text over a picture is hard to read: set backgroundOverlay (dim for light text, light for dark text) and give the text the matching color, or keep the text off the picture. Not on button, callout, ai_chat, approval_list, browser_view, pdf_compare or connector_status, which frame their own box.

backgroundFit.description: How the picture fills the box: cover, contain or tile. cover fills the box and crops the edges, contain shows the whole picture with room around it, tile repeats it at its own size (patterns, textures). Only has an effect together with backgroundImage. Not on button, callout, ai_chat, approval_list, browser_view, pdf_compare or connector_status, which frame their own box.

backgroundOverlay.description: A veil over the picture for readable content: none, dim or light. dim darkens the picture (for white text), light brightens it (for dark text). The validator warns about a picture without a veil under a component that shows text. Only has an effect together with backgroundImage. Not on button, callout, ai_chat, approval_list, browser_view, pdf_compare or connector_status, which frame their own box.

marginTop.description: Extra space above the component, in spacing steps. 0..8 steps of 4px times the theme density, added outside the box. Use it to set a block apart from the one above it instead of adding a spacer. Not on button, callout, ai_chat, approval_list, browser_view, pdf_compare or connector_status, which frame their own box.

marginBottom.description: Extra space below the component, in spacing steps. 0..8 steps of 4px times the theme density, added outside the box. Not on button, callout, ai_chat, approval_list, browser_view, pdf_compare or connector_status, which frame their own box.

shadow.description: Elevation of the component box: none, sm, md or lg. Uses the theme elevation tokens, which become outline rings in high contrast, so a raised box stays visible in every theme. Give the box a surface too (backgroundColor, or background "surface" on a card) or the shadow outlines bare content. Not on button, callout, ai_chat, approval_list, browser_view, pdf_compare or connector_status, which frame their own box.

opacity.description: How opaque the component is, from 10 to 100 percent. 100 changes nothing. Use it to quiet a secondary block, not to hide one (use visibility for that); text below about 60 gets hard to read. Not on button, callout, ai_chat, approval_list, browser_view, pdf_compare or connector_status, which frame their own box.

borderWidth.description: Border thickness in pixels, 1 to 4. Setting any of borderWidth, borderSides or borderColor draws a solid border on the box and replaces the border knob where the type has one. Without borderColor the border takes the theme border colour, without borderSides it goes all round. Not on button, callout, ai_chat, approval_list, browser_view, pdf_compare or connector_status, which frame their own box.

borderSides.description: Which sides get the border: all, top, right, bottom, left, x or y. x is left and right, y is top and bottom. One side with borderWidth 3 and a role colour makes an accent bar. Not on button, callout, ai_chat, approval_list, browser_view, pdf_compare or connector_status, which frame their own box.

borderColor.description: Border colour: a role or a #rrggbb colour. A role follows the theme in light, dark and high contrast, a hex colour stays exactly as written in every theme. Draws a border by itself (1px, all sides). Not on button, callout, ai_chat, approval_list, browser_view, pdf_compare or connector_status, which frame their own box.

backgroundColor.description: Fill of the component box: a role or a #rrggbb colour. Wins over the background knob where the type has one. A role paints a soft wash of that colour over the card surface, so text stays readable in light, dark and high contrast. A hex colour paints exactly that colour in every theme: the validator warns when the text on it would be hard to read, and a role is the safer choice. A card, stat or page_header with a look other than its default paints that look's own surface inside the box, so pick the look or this fill, not both. Most types have no padding knob, so text sits tight against the fill: put it in a card or container for an inset. Not on button, callout, ai_chat, approval_list, browser_view, pdf_compare or connector_status, which frame their own box.

columns.description: Number of equal columns of this grid, 12 when absent. Works on a section, card, container, form, tab, modal and repeater (the grid of each item). The children still size themselves with span, counted in these columns: with columns 5 a span of 1 is a fifth of the row and a span of 5 or more is the full row. Below 12 it also turns off the automatic tablet rule for this grid, so give children a spanMd where a tablet needs another split. Phones still stack.

responsive.description: Whether tablet-sized screens may rearrange the children of this grid. auto (the default): between 640 and 1023 px a child with span 1-4 takes half the row and 5-11 the full row. manual: every child keeps its span there unless it sets spanMd. Works on the same types as columns. Phones still stack unless a child sets spanSm.

hover.description: Reaction to the pointer: none, lift, tint, outline or grow. lift raises it a little with a shadow, tint washes it with the primary colour, outline rings it in the primary colour, grow scales it up by 2 percent. Use it on a block that is clickable (a card that opens a record, a stat that links on) so it reads as one, not on every block. It does nothing on touch screens, in the editor canvas or when the viewer asks for reduced motion, so never make it the only sign that something can be clicked.

spanMd.description: Width in columns on tablet-sized screens (640 to 1023 px wide). Absent: the automatic rule applies there (a span of 1-4 becomes half the row, 5-11 the full row), or the node keeps its span when the grid sets columns or responsive "manual". Counted in the columns of the parent grid, a value at or above that count is the full row.

spanSm.description: Width in columns on phones (narrower than 640 px). Absent: the node takes the full row, the phone stack every app has. Setting it on one child makes that grid keep its columns on a phone, and the children without spanSm still take a full row each. Use it for small things that fit side by side on a phone: two stats (6 and 6), an icon button beside a field (2 and 10).

rowSpan.description: How many grid rows the node covers. For a tall node beside shorter ones: a span-8 chart with rowSpan 2 next to two span-4 stats puts the stats above each other beside the chart. Does not work as a direct child of a section or container with height "fill", and is ignored where the grid stacks on a phone.

alignSelf.description: Vertical position of the node inside its grid row. stretch (the default) fills the height of the row, so cards in one row end at the same line. start, center and end keep the node at its own height at the top, middle or bottom of the row.

sticky.description: Keeps the node in view while the page scrolls past its row. It moves only inside its own grid row(s), so put it beside taller content: a span-4 summary card with sticky "top" next to a long span-8 form follows the scroll. Alone in a row it has nowhere to move. Not for a node inside a card, container or section with a fixed height (that box scrolls by itself). Off in the editor canvas.

stickyOffset.description: Distance a sticky node keeps from the edge, in spacing steps. Only read when sticky is "top" or "bottom". 0 (the default) sticks flush to the edge of the scrolling area.

font.description: Typeface role of the text: body, heading or mono. heading currently equals body. Use mono for codes, ids and amounts that should line up.

textSize.description: Exact text size from xs to 4xl, md is body size. auto keeps the size the component picks itself. A component that fixes the size of an inner part (a stat value) keeps that size, so use size on a stat instead.

lineHeight.description: Space between lines of text: tight, normal or relaxed. auto keeps the component default. Tight suits big headings, relaxed suits long paragraphs.

tracking.description: Space between letters: tight, normal or wide. auto keeps the component default. Wide together with transform uppercase makes a small label above a title.

transform.description: Letter case: none keeps what was typed, uppercase shows capitals. Keep uppercase for short labels, it is hard to read in long text.

events.description: Screen events: onOpen runs actions each time the screen opens. Shape { onOpen: "act_x" }, or a list of up to 5 action ids { onOpen: ["act_a", "act_b"] } that run one after the other and stop at the first that fails. It fires in the live app only (also after a navigate to this screen with other params), never in the editor or a screenshot. Use it to prepare the screen: set_variable to reset a filter, a refresh step, a dataset query into a resultVar. Do not use it for something a binding already loads by itself. On a public page it runs only actions of the public screens. Write it with app_update_screen { screenId, events: { onOpen: "act_…" } }, and events: null removes it. The same list form works on every component event slot (onClick, onSubmit, onChange, …) through app_bind_action.

timers.description: Timers that run an action every few seconds while the screen is open. everySeconds is 5 to 3600, at most 3 timers per screen, id is a short name (letters, digits, _ or -). A timer pauses while the browser tab is hidden and skips a tick while its previous run is still busy. It never runs in the editor or a screenshot. Only to reload the data on screen, use the screen's refreshInterval instead: a timer is for running an action, such as a check that writes a variable or a step that advances a status. Write the complete list with app_update_screen { screenId, timers: [{ id: "poll", everySeconds: 30, actionId: "act_…" }] }, and timers: null removes them.

accent.description: none = plain title; bar = a short primary accent bar beside the title; tinted = the title set in the app primary color.

text.label: Text
text.description: A paragraph of text. Supports a small markdown subset (bold, italic, links).

filter_bar.label: Filter bar
filter_bar.description: A row of filter controls (search, select, toggle, date). Each control writes vars.filters.<name>, for use in records-binding filter formulas.

kanban.label: Kanban
kanban.description: A kanban board over an array of objects, grouped into columns by groupByField and optionally into swimlanes by swimlaneField. Columns and swimlanes may be PINNED as literals or BOUND to a table (columnsSource/swimlanesSource) so the people using the app configure the board without opening the builder. Dragging a card fires onCardMove with { item, value, lane, index, beforeId, afterId } — enough to write both the new column and a new rank.
kanban.childrenDescription: Child components drawn per card in place of the built-in card body. Inside them item is the card's record and index its position, as in a repeater: bind with computed or formulas such as item.title. The card keeps its click and drag behaviour, so keep buttons out of a clickable card. No children means the built-in body (titleKey and the other keys). The phone draws the built-in body.

cardLook.description: default = the current flat card; tinted = soft primary wash on every card; raised = cards with shadow elevation.

record_detail.label: Record detail
record_detail.description: Labeled fields of ONE record — typically a {kind:"record"} binding whose filter uses screen.params (pairs with navigate params).

button.label: Button
button.description: A clickable button. Wire its onClick to an action; role "submit" submits the enclosing form.

variant.description: outline = transparent with a primary border and primary text; soft = filled with the soft primary tint, primary text.

disabledWhen.description: Truthy disables the button and blocks its action.

callout.label: Callout
callout.description: A highlighted note with a tone (info, success, warning, danger).

textFrom.description: Wins over `text` when it resolves to text.

toneFrom.description: Data-driven tone; a value outside the tone vocabulary falls back to `tone`.

stat.label: Stat
stat.description: A KPI tile: a label and a big value. The value can bind to an action result. v2 adds an optional delta/trend row.

captionSegments.description: Replaces caption: parts of one line, each colored by its tone.

look.description: plain = label and value only; tile = on its own card surface; tinted = soft primary wash; accent = tile with a primary edge bar; gradient = soft primary gradient wash, value in the primary color.

formatOptions.description: How the tile writes its value and its delta when they are numbers. An object { currency?: "USD", decimals?: 0..10, pattern?: "dd-MM-yyyy", compact?: true, percentScale?: "whole"|"fraction" }, every key optional, set only what should differ. A numeric value is written as an amount when currency is set (or as a percentage when percentScale is set), as a number otherwise; text values are shown as they are. The delta follows deltaFormat and takes decimals and compact. currency (ISO 4217) and decimals win over the app-level `format`. compact writes 1.2K / 3.4M. percentScale "fraction" reads 0.25 as 25% (the default "whole" reads 25 as 25%). pattern is a date pattern from yyyy yy MMMM MMM MM M dd d EEEE EEE HH H hh h mm ss a, literal letters in single quotes. Absent keeps the default way of writing the value.

table.label: Table
table.description: A table over an array of objects — usually an automation result. Missing keys render as “—”.

formatOptions.description: How this column writes its numbers, amounts and dates. An object { currency?: "USD", decimals?: 0..10, pattern?: "dd-MM-yyyy", compact?: true, percentScale?: "whole"|"fraction" }, every key optional, set only what should differ. It applies to the number, currency, percent, progress, date, datetime and relative formats of the column. currency (ISO 4217) and decimals win over the app-level `format`. compact writes 1.2K / 3.4M. percentScale "fraction" reads 0.25 as 25% (the default "whole" reads 25 as 25%). pattern is a date pattern from yyyy yy MMMM MMM MM M dd d EEEE EEE HH H hh h mm ss a, literal letters in single quotes. Absent keeps the default way of writing the value.

look.description: default = the current ruled table; striped = zebra rows; minimal = borderless, whitespace-separated rows.

pagination.description: Pages through a records source: loadMore appends, prevNext steps pages. A page is the source's limit rows and rowLimit does not cut it. Left out, the table shows the one page the source reads.

data_grid.label: Data grid
data_grid.description: A powerful table over an array of objects: sortable/filterable columns, paging, selection, search and row actions.

formatOptions.description: How this column writes its numbers, amounts and dates. An object { currency?: "USD", decimals?: 0..10, pattern?: "dd-MM-yyyy", compact?: true, percentScale?: "whole"|"fraction" }, every key optional, set only what should differ. It applies to the number, currency, percent, progress, date, datetime and relative formats of the column. currency (ISO 4217) and decimals win over the app-level `format`. compact writes 1.2K / 3.4M. percentScale "fraction" reads 0.25 as 25% (the default "whole" reads 25 as 25%). pattern is a date pattern from yyyy yy MMMM MMM MM M dd d EEEE EEE HH H hh h mm ss a, literal letters in single quotes. Absent keeps the default way of writing the value.

groupBy.description: Column key to group rows under collapsible header rows.

groupOrder.description: Group order; unlisted values follow in data order. collapsed:true starts a group closed.

activeWhen.description: Formula per row (item, index in scope); a match highlights the row as active.

look.description: default = the current ruled grid; striped = zebra rows; minimal = borderless rows; cards = each row rendered as its own card.

pagination.description: loadMore adds the next page of a records source under the grid. A page is the source's limit rows and pageSize keeps paging the rows the grid holds. Left out, the grid shows the one page the source reads.

chart.label: Chart
chart.description: A bar/line/area/pie/donut chart over an array of objects. x-axis from xKey, one or more series by key. xType:"time" spaces points by date rather than evenly, so a gap in the data reads as a gap. referenceLines/referenceBands draw a target or healthy range behind the series; unitLabel suffixes the axis and tooltip. onRowClick fires with the clicked row.

orientation.description: bar only: horizontal = categories on the Y axis, value labels right of the bars.

formatOptions.description: How the value axis and the tooltip write the numbers of this chart. An object { currency?: "USD", decimals?: 0..10, pattern?: "dd-MM-yyyy", compact?: true, percentScale?: "whole"|"fraction" }, every key optional, set only what should differ. It refines valueFormat (number, currency or percent): pattern does not apply here, and unitLabel is still written after the number. currency (ISO 4217) and decimals win over the app-level `format`. compact writes 1.2K / 3.4M. percentScale "fraction" reads 0.25 as 25% (the default "whole" reads 25 as 25%). pattern is a date pattern from yyyy yy MMMM MMM MM M dd d EEEE EEE HH H hh h mm ss a, literal letters in single quotes. Absent keeps the default way of writing the value.

list.label: List
list.childrenDescription: Child components drawn per row in place of the built-in row body. Inside them item is the row's record and index its position, as in a repeater: bind with computed or formulas such as item.title. The row keeps its click and behaviour, so keep buttons out of a clickable row. No children means the built-in body (titleKey and the other keys). The phone draws the built-in body.
list.description: A card list over an array of objects — a friendlier alternative to a table, and the natural sidebar picker. badgeToneMap colours a status pill the way sideMap does for a message thread; timestampKey shows a short relative time; unreadKey bolds the row; tagsKey shows a tags field (e.g. mail categories) as chips.

look.description: rows = the current flat row list; cards = each item on its own card surface; tiles = a compact multi-column tile grid.

peekSource.description: Rows related to the list rows — joined per row on peekMatchKey. An aggregate keeps it small on a long table.

pagination.description: Pages through a records source: loadMore appends, prevNext steps pages. A page is the source's limit rows. Left out, the list shows the one page the source reads.

card.label: Card
card.description: A surface that groups other components. Children lay out on the card’s own 12-column grid.

look.description: default = the current card surface; flat = flush and borderless; raised = shadow elevation; tinted = soft primary wash; accent = a primary edge bar; gradient = soft primary gradient surface; solid = filled with the primary colour, contents in its contrast colour (title colour: heading color knob).

form.label: Form
form.description: Groups inputs and submits them to an action. Renders one built-in submit button; set showSubmit false for a form whose fields save on change.

validateOn.description: When field errors show. Default is on submit; blur checks a field when it loses focus, change on every edit.

ai_chat.label: AI chat
ai_chat.description: A chat surface the app's viewers can talk to. Runs on the app OWNER's model tier (acts-as-owner) and can be grounded in the owner's knowledge bases. `mode:"assistant"` answers one question at a time instead of keeping a conversation.

temperature.description: How much the answer may vary between runs, a number from 0 to 2. Use 0 to 0.3 for extraction, classification and anything checked, 0.7 or more for free drafts. Leave it out to keep the model tier's own setting (most steps should).

checks.description: Rules every answer must pass before the step succeeds. A list (at most 20) of { kind, field, ... }. field is a path in the answer: a schema field of ai_generate with a schema ("category"), "text" for a plain ai_generate, "rows[].category" for ai_extract. Kinds: allowedFrom { ref, value?, ignoreCase?, allowEmpty? } (the answer is one of the list at ref, value names the key of each list item that holds the allowed value), numbersFrom { ref, tolerance?, ignoreUpTo?, percent?, ignoreDates? } (every number in the answer appears in the data at ref: no invented amounts), script { script, minRatio? } (written in latin, cyrillic, greek, arabic, hebrew, han, japanese, hangul, devanagari or thai), items { minItems?, maxItems?, sameCountAs? } (a list of the right length, sameCountAs a list path). ref and sameCountAs are paths into the step's own data: form.<input>, vars.<name>, item.<field>, params.<name> or value, no {{ }} and never secrets. A failing answer goes back to the AI with what failed (repairRounds), after that the step fails with ai_check_failed. Leave it out for no checks.

repairRounds.description: Extra AI calls that fix an answer which failed its checks. A whole number from 0 to 3, only read when the step has checks. Leave it out for 1 round. Each round sends what failed back to the AI and costs one more AI call. 0 fails the step at the first failed check.

onSuccess.description: A toast and/or a screen to open after the sequence ends well. Effects are applied once and never chain, so use steps for anything longer. Same shape as on run_automation.

onError.description: A toast and/or a screen to open after the sequence failed. The failure is toasted either way. Effects are applied once and never chain.

screenExpr.description: A formula that gives the id of the screen to open, instead of screenId. It must return the id of one of this app's own screens, any other result stops the sequence with an error. Leave screenId out when you use it.

messageExpr.description: A formula that gives the message text, instead of message. Build the text with concat, for example concat('Saved ', vars.count, ' rows'). When it returns nothing, message is shown if there is one. Leave message out when you use it.

urlExpr.description: A formula that gives the web address to open, instead of url. Only https addresses on a host listed in the app's allowedLinkHosts open, anything else stops the sequence with an error. Leave url out when you use it.

messageExpr.description: A formula that gives the question text, instead of message. When it returns nothing, message is shown if there is one. Leave message out when you use it.

titleExpr.description: A formula that gives the dialog title, instead of title. When it returns nothing, title is used if there is one.

confirmLabelExpr.description: A formula for the confirm button text, instead of confirmLabel. When it returns nothing, confirmLabel is used if there is one.

cancelLabelExpr.description: A formula for the cancel button text, instead of cancelLabel. When it returns nothing, cancelLabel is used if there is one.

inputMapping.description: Per automation input, where its value comes from: {kind:"static",value}, {kind:"field",name,formId?} or, since version 3, {kind:"formula",expr}. A formula is worked out on the server when the automation starts, from the roots a server step has (form, vars, item, index, value, params, currentUser, now, today), so it can send a variable, the loop item or a computed value. Only on a run_automation STEP of a sequence: a run_automation action on its own takes static and field.

guard.description: Skips the step on the server when this formula is false. The server works it out before it runs the step. When it gives false or nothing, or cannot be worked out, the step is skipped: nothing is written or sent, its result is null and the sequence goes on. Use it for a rule the browser must not be able to switch off, for example currentUser.roleKey == "manager" or form.amount <= 500. A condition step decides in the browser, a guard decides on the server. It reads the roots a server step has (form, vars, item, index, value, params, currentUser, now, today), and screen, forms and actions only when the app sets serverScope to "wide". Only currentUser comes from the server: every other root is sent by the browser, so decide who may do something with currentUser, never with vars, form or actions. A guard covers its own step only, so each step that needs the rule carries it. Every server step kind takes it, the kinds added later too. A step inside a transaction takes no guard of its own: put it on the transaction.

A failing answer goes back to the AI with what failed (repairRounds), after that the step fails with ai_check_failed. Leave it out for no checks.

repairRounds.description: Extra AI calls that fix an answer which failed its checks. A whole number from 0 to 3, only read when the step has checks. Leave it out for 1 round. Each round sends what failed back to the AI and costs one more AI call. 0 fails the step at the first failed check.

guard.description: Skips the step on the server when this formula is false. The server works it out before it runs the step. When it gives false or nothing, or cannot be worked out, the step is skipped: nothing is written or sent, its result is null and the sequence goes on. Use it for a rule the browser must not be able to switch off, for example currentUser.roleKey == "manager" or form.amount <= 500. A condition step decides in the browser, a guard decides on the server. It reads the roots a server step has (form, vars, item, index, value, params, currentUser, now, today), and screen, forms and actions only when the app sets serverScope to "wide". Only currentUser comes from the server: every other root is sent by the browser, so decide who may do something with currentUser, never with vars, form or actions. A guard covers its own step only, so each step that needs the rule carries it. Every server step kind takes it, the kinds added later too. A step inside a transaction takes no guard of its own: put it on the transaction.

temperature.description: How much the answer may vary between runs, a number from 0 to 2. Use 0 to 0.3 for extraction, classification and anything checked, 0.7 or more for free drafts. Leave it out to keep the model tier's own setting (most steps should).

text.description: What is copied: { kind: "static", value } or a formula. A number or a list is copied as text.

nodeId.description: The id of the component to focus.

connectorId.description: The id of a `rest` connector of this app (app_list_connectors lists them). It fixes the host and the credential.

method.description: GET reads. POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE change something on the other side.

path.description: The path on the connector's host, starting with "/". {{form.x}}, {{vars.x}}, {{item.x}} and {{params.x}} are filled in URL-encoded. No "?" or "#" (use `query`).

query.description: Query parameters: { <name>: binding }. A list sends the name once per item, an empty value is left out.

headers.description: Extra request headers: { <name>: binding }. Authorization, Cookie and the headers the connector sets are refused.

body.description: The request body of a POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE. A static value is a template: a record, list or JSON text whose text values may hold {{form.x}}, {{vars.x}}, {{item.x}}, {{params.x}} (a value that is exactly one placeholder keeps its type). A formula or field binding is sent as the value it yields.

bodyFormat.description: How `body` is sent: json (application/json), form (application/x-www-form-urlencoded) or text (text/plain).

expect.description: How the answer is read: json (parsed, an empty answer is null) or text.

idempotencyKey.description: A value that names this one write (an order id, a uuid from an earlier step). Sent as the Idempotency-Key header, and what makes `retry` allowed on a write.

resultVar.description: The variable that gets { status, body }.

guard.description: Skips the step on the server when this formula is false. The server works it out before it runs the step. When it gives false or nothing, or cannot be worked out, the step is skipped: nothing is written or sent, its result is null and the sequence goes on. Use it for a rule the browser must not be able to switch off, for example currentUser.roleKey == "manager" or form.amount <= 500. A condition step decides in the browser, a guard decides on the server. It reads the roots a server step has (form, vars, item, index, value, params, currentUser, now, today), and screen, forms and actions only when the app sets serverScope to "wide". Only currentUser comes from the server: every other root is sent by the browser, so decide who may do something with currentUser, never with vars, form or actions. A guard covers its own step only, so each step that needs the rule carries it. Every server step kind takes it, the kinds added later too. A step inside a transaction takes no guard of its own: put it on the transaction.

branches.description: The branches, 1 to 8: [{ steps: [...] }, { steps: [...] }]. Each branch is its own list of steps.

failFast.description: true: when one branch fails, the other branches stop before their next step. Left out or false: every branch runs to its end first.

message.description: What went wrong, for the person: a static text or a formula (at most 500 characters are shown).

code.description: A short machine name for the failure, read as error.code by a catch ("raised" when left out).

value.description: The result of the action: a static value or a formula. Left out, the result stays what the last server step gave.

nodeId.description: The id of the component to scroll to, or "top" for the top of the screen.

form.description: The form, by name: its props.name, or its node id when it has no name (the key reset_form takes).

field.description: The input inside that form, by its props.name.

value.description: The new value: { kind: "static", value } or { kind: "formula", expr }.

nodeId.description: The id of the tabs, modal or data_grid component.

state.description: Which state: activeTab (a tabs group), open (a modal) or selection (a data_grid).

value.description: The new state: a tab id or 0-based position, true or false, or the row id(s) to select.

catch.description: Runs when a step in `steps` fails, with error.message, error.step, error.code and error.attempts in scope. Present (even empty): the failure is handled and the action goes on. Left out: the failure still ends the action after `finally`.

finally.description: Always runs last: after `steps` succeeded, after `catch`, and before a return, break or continue leaves the try.

seconds.description: How long to pause, in whole seconds (1 to 30).

expr.description: Checked before every round. The steps run while it is true.

maxIterations.description: The most rounds that run (1 to 200, 200 when left out). When it is reached the loop ends and the action goes on.
